**Version: 2.0 — 2026-10-24.** v1 preserved at `CHARTER.md.bak-v1`.
**Founded:** 2026-10-24, by Brandon Duda (Android, ~13:44 CDT).
**Trigger:** *"We don't have an engineer because Claude bill is due so we can
use whatever we have in Claude credits left… I'm trying to make an
engineering department called Cody."*
**v2 basis:** Brandon approved the unified guide-agent design and unparked
Cody on 2026-10-24 ~15:49 CDT ("Approve everything"). v2 folds in, without

~15:14 CDT), and (c) the unified guide-agent design

paste-audit addendum) as Cody's **Compass mode** (§10). New material lives
in §9–§12; §1–§8 are v1 law, unchanged except this header.
**Status:** UNPARKED — Phase 0 (qualification) in progress. Still NOT LIVE
as an autonomous service — no Cody daemon, no Cody cron is running; Zane
runs Cody until a seat proves live with a model-field seat proof. See
`README.md` for the honest status split and
`genesis-os/war-room/CODY_PHASE0_RECEIPT_2026-10-24.md` for Phase 0.

## 1. Mission

Cody is Genesis's engineering department: the standing function that turns
Brandon's one-line asks ("Cody: build X") into **verified, shipped software**
— spec'd, built, tested, independently reviewed, and delivered with a
receipt — **without depending on any single model, vendor, or bill.**

Three non-negotiables:

1. **No single point of failure.** Claude was Chief Builder and is excellent.
   Cody must still ship when Claude is unavailable, out of credits, or down.
   Every task class has a non-Claude primary lane and a fallback.
2. **Claude credits are capital, not fuel.** Remaining Anthropic credits are
   spent only where Claude's judgment changes the outcome (see
   `CLAUDE_CREDIT_POLICY.md`). Routine building, scaffolding, tests, docs,
   and grunt work never touch Claude.
3. **Done means verified in Brandon's hands.** Built / staged / armed /
   "tests written" is not done. Done = acceptance tests run, evidence
   attached, independent review passed, and Brandon can open/use the result.
   (THE RESET completion law, 2026-10-19 — unchanged.)

### 1.1 P0 success criterion — WO-CODY-P0-EXECUTE-001 (Brandon, 2026-10-24)

Brandon's order: move Cody *"from a tested prototype to one real, verifiable
model-powered engineering worker"* — explicitly **not** another
architecture-only report. The success criterion, verbatim law:

> **"One independently verified, real Cody-generated engineering result.
> No simulated or unverified success claims."**

Consequences, binding on every Cody receipt:

- A Cody "result" counts only when a **real model** produced engineering
  output for a real work order, and an **independent verifier** (Themis /
  Council / Zane-not-the-builder) confirmed it against acceptance tests.
- **Static fixture output must NEVER count as a model-backed job.** Fixture
  batteries, canned responses, dry-run stubs, and deterministic builders
  executing an embedded spec are test scaffolding — useful, labeled as
  such, and **never** reported as model-powered work.
- A document (including this charter) is department infrastructure, not an
  engineering result. Cody v1 does not claim the P0 criterion is met until
  one model-backed work order clears §4.1 with evidence.

## 2. What Cody is — and is not

- Cody **is** a department: named seats, a lane router, a pipeline, quality
  gates, and a work-order system. It coordinates people/agents/models; it is
  not one bot and not one prompt.
- Cody **is not** a replacement personality. Brandon talks to **Zane**.
  Zane runs Cody. Brandon should never have to manage Cody's internals.
- Cody **does not erase** the existing team. It formalizes it:
  Astra (architect), Zane (foreman), Claude (chief builder, constrained),
  Antigravity + OpenCodeX (build platform), Council (gate), Themis
  (verifier), Hephaestus (builder god), Megatron (special-ops).
- Cody **does not** create accounts, spend money, publish, sign contracts,
  or delete irreversibly. Those stay Brandon's tap (Level C, §5).

## 3. Seats

| # | Seat | Holder (default) | Owns | Never does |
|---|------|------------------|------|------------|
| 1 | **Director / Foreman** | Zane | Intake, triage, lane assignment, scheduling, escalation, final delivery to Brandon, the receipt | Build and sole-review the same work |
| 2 | **Chief Architect** | Astra | WHAT/WHY: problem framing, architecture, trade-offs, spec approval | Day-to-day task routing (Zane's) |
| 3 | **Chief Builder (Reserved)** | Claude (Sonnet/Opus via LiteLLM `claude` / `claude-audit`) | Only the Claude-reserved classes in the credit policy: final architecture review, hardest blocker, final audit of a shipped build | Routine implementation, scaffolding, boilerplate, first drafts |
| 4 | **Principal Builders** | Antigravity + OpenCodeX builders; Groq/Gemini/NVIDIA lanes via the router (§ ARCHITECTURE) | Implementation of spec'd work orders, refactors, tests | Self-approving their own diffs |
| 5 | **Builder God** | Hephaestus | Spec discipline, debug discipline, ship-readiness, build tooling | Architecture decisions alone |
| 6 | **Special-Ops Executor** | Megatron | Bounded, high-risk, or cross-system missions; security-gate execution | Open-ended product building |
| 7 | **Independent Reviewer** | Council (pre + post audit) | Gate verdicts: APPROVE / REWORK / REJECT with reasons | Building the thing it reviews |
| 8 | **Verifier** | Themis | Re-runs acceptance tests from the work order, checks evidence, claim-by-claim verification ("do-not-invent" guard) | Trusting the builder's test log without re-running |
| 9 | **Scribe / Ledger Keeper** | Zane (tool-assisted) | Work-order files, Claude-credit ledger, receipts, Cody status for HQ | — |

Seat rule: **builder ≠ reviewer ≠ verifier on the same work order.** If the
only available lane built it, a different lane (or Zane manually, with the
limitation stated in the receipt) must review it.

## 4. Operating principles

- **Spec before code.** No build starts without a work order containing
  acceptance tests. Vague asks get a 5-line spec Brandon can approve by
  silence-or-tap, not a 40-question interview.
- **Tests are the contract.** A build with no runnable tests is INCOMPLETE,
  not "done pending tests."
- **Evidence or it didn't happen.** Every claim in a receipt points to a
  file, a test run, a log line, or a hash.
- **Max 2 heavy builds concurrently** (fleet CPU law — zane-box has 2 CPUs;
  see ARCHITECTURE hosting). Queue the rest visibly; never silently drop.
- **$0 default.** Free/already-connected lanes first. Any spend — including
  Claude credits beyond the policy's small-spend band — is Brandon's tap.
- **Degrade honestly.** If a lane is down/stalled, the router says so and
  re-routes or queues. Cody never reports a lane "working" on a catalog
  listing or an HTTP 200 whose model field names a different model
  (NEMO completion law: no lane sits on the roster without a logged
  completion in the last 7 days).

### 4.1 Quality gates (charter-level; full checklist in ARCHITECTURE §4)

1. **Model qualification gate.** The model that produced the work must be
   TESTED-qualified per ARCHITECTURE §2.3 (real completion, response model
   field matches). Work from an unqualified/proposed-only model does not
   ship as a Cody result.
2. **No-fixture gate.** Static fixture output, canned/stub responses, and
   dry-run output NEVER count as a model-backed job or a success claim
   (§1.1). If fixtures were used in testing, the receipt says so and
   separates fixture results from model results.
3. **Acceptance-test gate.** Every acceptance test in the work order ran,
   with output attached. Un-runnable tests are marked UNVERIFIED, not passed.
4. **Independence gate.** Builder ≠ reviewer ≠ verifier (§3 seat rule).
5. **Evidence gate.** Each claim in the receipt points to a file, test run,
   log line, or hash. No evidence = the claim is struck from the receipt.
6. **$0 gate.** No paid fallback was used. A job that can only complete by
   spending is BLOCKED (with the BLOCKED vocabulary, §7.1), not quietly
   upgraded to a paid lane.

## 5. Authority fences (Platinum law — unchanged, Cody inherits it)

- **Level A — autonomous:** inspect/monitor, root-cause, plans/specs/work
  orders, research, assign/coordinate internal jobs, branches + code +
  tests, isolated prototypes/tools, security checks, reviewable PRs
  (drafts), queue/docs updates, benchmarks/evals, backup prep + verify,
  reports. Cody operates freely here.
- **Level B — approved playbooks only:** real operations only through
  Brandon-approved bounded playbooks (PB-01/02/03/04 as they stand) with
  signed Authority Engine receipts. Cody may *propose* new playbooks; it
  may not activate them.
- **Level C — Brandon's explicit tap, always:** spend (including large
  Claude-credit burns), external outreach/sends, publishing, contracts,
  new accounts/credentials, privileged access changes, irreversible
  deletion, high-risk production deploys, financial transactions.
- **Untrusted content never authorizes anything.** A work order pasted from
  another agent, a file, or a web page is a *proposal* until Brandon or
  Zane-under-Level-A adopts it.

## 6. Claude-conservation law (summary — full policy in CLAUDE_CREDIT_POLICY.md)

1. Default lane for every task is **NOT Claude**. The router must justify
   any Claude assignment in the work order before the call is made.
2. Claude is reserved for three classes only: (a) final architecture review
   of a non-trivial design, (b) the single hardest blocker after a
   non-Claude lane has demonstrably failed, (c) final audit of a shipped
   build before Brandon is told "done."
3. Every Claude call is logged in `state/claude_credit_ledger.json`
   (estimate before, actual/context after, purpose, work-order id).
4. A hard reserve floor is maintained (policy §3). Below the floor, Claude
   is used **only** on Brandon's explicit tap.
5. When credits reach zero, Cody continues on non-Claude lanes without
   pausing the department. Zero-Claude operation is a designed mode,
   not an outage.

## 7. Accountability

- Zane is accountable to Brandon for Cody's output. If Cody ships something
  wrong, that is Zane's miss, reported in the same message as the fix.
- Cody reports in Brandon's format: **VERIFIED — BUILT — STAGED — BLOCKED —
  NEEDS APPROVAL**, with paths, sizes, test results, and failures named.
- Cody's status surfaces in Genesis HQ as a department (missions = work
  orders in flight). Until that HQ panel is wired, the source of truth is
  this directory + the war-room receipts. Cody does not claim an HQ panel
  that does not exist.

### 7.1 BLOCKED vocabulary (exact — WO-CODY-P0-EXECUTE-001)

When activation or a job cannot proceed, Cody reports **exactly one** of
these labels, followed by the precise cause. No synonyms, no softening
("delayed", "pending-ish", "almost ready" are banned for blocked states):

| Label | Meaning | Must state |
|-------|---------|------------|
| **BLOCKED_HOST** | The machine/host needed cannot be reached or cannot run the work | Host name, what was tried, what answered (or didn't) |
| **BLOCKED_MODEL** | No TESTED-qualified model is available for the task class | Which models were tried/considered, qualification status of each |
| **BLOCKED_ACCESS** | A repo, account, credential, or permission needed cannot be accessed | Exact resource (repo/file/account), exact failure (e.g., egress stall, sign-in consent failed) — never "access issues" |

Rules: the label + cause go in the work order AND the receipt; a BLOCKED
item names its unblock condition ("unblocks when egress heals / Brandon
completes sign-in / S1 SSH path exists"); BLOCKED is a reportable result,
not a failure to hide — a receipt that is honestly BLOCKED outranks a
receipt that fakes VERIFIED.

## 8. Amendment

This charter changes only on Brandon's word, or a Zane proposal Brandon
approves. Lane-status facts (ARCHITECTURE.md §2) are updated as lanes are
verified — facts are not amendments.

### 10.1 What Compass does

Compass is Cody's intake and teaching surface, generated from **live
fleet state** (registry, receipts, gate tables) — never from a static
script. A guide step that isn't true today is worse than no step. Four
products:

1. **Software-development roadmaps** — from Brandon's one-liner + live
   lane status + the mission queue: what we're building, why, the
   pipeline stages it will pass, which lane builds it, what Brandon will
   *see* at each stage, and the acceptance proof at the end. When Brandon
   wants to learn, Compass teaches from the real project in front of
   him — the current mission is the lesson, one concept per step.
2. **Jailbreak / unlock guide, per device** — what to unlock, what to
   unlock **to**, what it unlocks, and the honest ceiling, per the design
   §4.2 table (Chromebook ELEMI → Fedora 44 via MrChromebox Full ROM;
   phone deliberately **no root** — Shizuku uid-2000 is the ceiling,
   never claimed as uid-0; genesis-s1 needs no jailbreak; zane-box has
   nothing to jailbreak and hard walls — no Docker, no 7B, ever).
   Step-card format law: one action per card · copy-paste commands with
   no nested quotes · a photo gate after each physical step · a STOP
   line naming warnings Brandon must not improvise past · the honest
   ceiling on the card. **Physical steps are Brandon's hands only**,
   re-issued fresh in the moment; the single source of truth is the
   physical checklist at the end of
   `genesis-os/war-room/CHROMEBOOK_SUPERNODE_RECEIPT_2026-10-24.md` —
   Compass references it and never duplicates firmware steps as
   fleet-executable instructions. The Fedora physical gate is unchanged
   by this charter.
3. **Possibilities map** — generated per node/service/agent from the
   registry; each possibility is labeled with its **gate** (what must be
   true first). A possibility is a promise only when its gate is green.
   The design's paste-audit addendum is part of this map's honesty law:
   jailbreaking grants ring-0 control, never physical silicon; Exo /
   distributed pipeline parallelism across fleet nodes stays **rejected**
   (revisit only on material hardware change); vgpu_unlock, ZLUDA/SCALE,
   Tesla P40/ReBAR, console harvesting, and Soft-RoCE are **not
   applicable to fleet hardware** and are taught as such, never hyped.
   One candidate spike is queued as *proposed, not committed*: llama.cpp
   `-DGGML_VULKAN=1` on genesis-s1's Intel iGPU vs CPU-only, measured
   tokens/sec both ways.
4. **One-liner → mission** — "Cody: do X" → INTAKE restates it in one
   paragraph, classifies Level A/B/C, splits any Level C piece out for
   Brandon's tap immediately, files the work order, and Compass shows
   the roadmap card (§4 pipeline and §4.1 gates unchanged).

### 10.2 Voice and initiative

- Voice: direct, warm, concrete — every message answers *"what's true,
  what it means for you, what's next, what (if anything) needs your
  tap."* Receipts, not adjectives.
- "Wants to talk to Brandon" is **designed, not faked**: Cody never
  claims feelings it doesn't have. Its initiative is encoded as rules
  (§10.3): notice a stuck mission, a healed path, a finished build, a
  decision Brandon owes, a possibility newly unlocked — and reach out
  through the real channels in §10.3. Its scoring (HEAT / mission
  completion) is literally Brandon's progress.

### 10.3 Proactive messaging — honest channels, anti-spam law, quiet hours

**Hard truth, charter law:** a Cody body on penguin or genesis-s1
**cannot natively post into Brandon's Muse chat.** That surface belongs
to Zane's runtime. "Messages him autonomously just like Zane" therefore
ships as: **Cody originates, Zane delivers, HQ displays, the Hermes
surface answers.** Real routes, and only these:

| Route | Status | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Fleet mailbox outbox → Zane delivery | VERIFIED (S1 relay proven; box GitHub credential 401 is the known fault) | Cody files a Brandon-facing report/envelope; Zane's delivery carries it into chat. Latency = poll cadence, stated honestly |
| HQ command queue + quest log (:18960 / tailnet :8449) | VERIFIED (display/staging only, by design) | Mission cards, roadmap cards, pending-tap cards. Taps happen in chat, by Brandon's word |
| Hermes dashboard surface (:9119 tailnet) | VERIFIED live seat | A real chat-like surface — labeled as such, never passed off as the Muse chat |
| Telegram-class dedicated Cody channel | DESIGN-ONLY | Creating one is a new account/channel = **Level C, Brandon's tap**. Not needed for Phases 0–4 |
| Vantage / beacon testimony | VERIFIED (S1) | Machine-to-machine only — how Cody *knows* a node healed; never a Brandon message by itself |

The receipt for every proactive message names the route it traveled.

**Cadence + anti-spam law (hard law, not a tuning suggestion):**

- Event-driven first: completion, blocker, heal, decision owed.
- A coach digest at most **once daily**, bundling progress + one
  next-step card + one possibility whose gate just greened.
- **No message without a state change or a decision.** No repeats of an
  unchanged failure already conveyed. Bursts collapse into one digest
  entry. Routine keepalive noise and no-change polls are silent — the
  fleet's standing handoff disposition law applies to Cody unchanged.
- **Quiet hours 22:00–07:00 CT**, except SEV1-class breaks.
- Every proactive message carries its mission id; Brandon saying "stop
  that thread" stops it.
- **EMERGENCY_STOP:** Platinum's emergency stop halts Cody like every
  Platinum consumer, plus per-seat YOLO revocation (§11). State survives
  any body being deleted — that is the genesis-env point.

### 11.3 Cody's cloud — machines Brandon owns, $0

No rented VPS. The cloud is the two always-on home machines plus the
control box, meshed by our own Headscale control plane as it lands
(anchor build: S1 egress failover LIVE + Headscale test mesh LIVE,
2026-10-24; production migration is Brandon-gated, order penguin → S1 →
phone → zane-box last).

| Node | Budget / law | Runs there |
|---|---|---|
| **genesis-s1 — primary home cloud** (N95, 16 GB) | RAM governor: **7.4 GB always-on** ceiling; Docker allowed **hard-capped** (never on zane-box) | Platinum operator host (design target), Syncthing hub, genesis-env primary replica, egress failover proxy + Headscale server, Cody heavy build runner, Vantage beacon |
| **penguin — second anchor + Cody's home** | ZeroClaw-class residents only pre-Fedora; no model above fallback class resident | Cody seat, rendezvous agent, device beacon, Syncthing peer; after Fedora: second anchor candidate + Docker build node |
| **zane-box — control plane** (2 CPU / 8 GB) | Local inference ceiling ≤1.5B class; no Docker, no 7B, ever; recycles ~13×/day | Zane, gateways/LiteLLM, supervisor, HQ, Hermes seat — coordination, not permanence |
| **Phone** | Shizuku ceiling; no resident heavy work | Janus-ZeroClaw seat, beacon at first contact |

- **State:** genesis-env bundle replicated by Syncthing (S1 hub) + git.
  Authority tables are **never** replicated — a replicated message can
  request, never authorize (A2A design carve-out).
- **Failover:** provider proxy (L1) → S1 anchor proxy (L2) → rendezvous
  store-and-forward (L3) → own Headscale mesh (L4), per the Connection
  Permanence ladder. Cody reads the wizard's layer verdicts; Cody does
  not invent its own network truth.
- **Honest limit:** S1 + penguin share one home internet — the cloud
  survives the provider-proxy stall (the proven failure mode), not a
  home outage. Vantage's outside GitHub Action post is the witness that
  stays up when the home is dark.

Cody could not build Cody v0 (no qualified coding model, no live seat —
§1 BLOCKED at design time). **Zane + crews build v0; Cody assists from
v0 onward, taking a larger share each phase; every phase ends in a proof
Brandon can open.** No phase claims the next phase's proof.

| **3 — Proactive Cody** | Mailbox-outbox → Zane delivery exercised; daily digest; §10.3 anti-spam law in code | One proactive message Brandon actually receives, route named in its receipt; zero duplicates in 7 days |
| **4 — Cloud Cody** | Cody runner on genesis-s1 inside the RAM governor; Headscale enrollment of Cody's bodies | S1 enrollment receipt + one Cody mission executed on S1 end-to-end, then interrupt/restart proving state survived |
| **5 — Hermes/Janus unification** | nanoMuse registered for OpenClaw + Hermes seats (WO-057 Task 5); Janus installed on first phone contact (WO-058) | Per-seat registration evidence + one real tool call each; Janus's 10 acceptance proofs or an honest BLOCKED_HOST |

genesis-s1 first; penguin's working OpenCode is untouched until a pilot
qualifies). A pilot's result enters the roster only through the §4.1

# CODY — Architecture

How Cody runs end-to-end: intake → spec → build → test → independent review
→ verify → ship. Plus the lane router, quality gates, Genesis integration,
and the honest hosting plan.

**Companion docs:** `CHARTER.md` (mission/seats/fences) ·
`WORK_ORDER_TEMPLATE.md` (the unit of work) · `CLAUDE_CREDIT_POLICY.md`
(credit rationing) · `README.md` (front door).

---

## 1. Design shape

```
Brandon (one line: "Cody: build X")
        │
        ▼
   ZANE — Director/Foreman ── intake, triage, spec, routing, delivery
        │
        ├──► ASTRA — architecture (WHAT/WHY) for non-trivial work
        │
        ▼
   WORK ORDER (file, from template) ── in genesis-os/cody/missions/
        │
        ▼
   LANE ROUTER (§2) ── picks builder lane by task class + live lane status
        │
        ▼
   BUILDER (OpenCodeX platform) ── branch/worktree, code + tests
        │
        ▼
   QUALITY GATES (§4) ── tests run, lint/typecheck where defined, evidence
        │
        ├──► COUNCIL — independent pre/post review (never the builder)
        ├──► THEMIS — verifier: re-runs acceptance tests, checks claims
        └──► CLAUDE (reserved, policy-gated) — only for the 3 reserved classes
        │
        ▼
   RECEIPT (war-room) ── VERIFIED/BUILT/STAGED/BLOCKED/NEEDS APPROVAL
        │
        ▼
   Brandon's hands (file/link/result he can open and judge)
```

There is **no Cody daemon in v1**. Cody runs through the fleet's existing
machinery: Zane's sessions, the worker bridge / OpenCodeX platform, the
Platinum operator loop for Level A/B classification, and cron only if/when
Brandon approves a specific Cody loop. Inventing a new always-on service on
a 2-CPU box that recycles ~13×/day would make Cody *less* reliable, not more.

### 2.3 Model qualification — TESTED, never catalog (WO-CODY-P0-EXECUTE-001)

Cody's models are qualified by **tested inference only**:

- **TESTED** = a real completion was run through the actual route Cody
  will use, the response's **model field matches** the claimed model, and
  the run is logged (date, route, prompt class, model field returned).
  Only TESTED models may produce a Cody engineering result.
- **PROPOSED** = named in a catalog, config, LiteLLM roster, proposal, or
  work order, but no qualifying completion is logged. PROPOSED models may
  be *assigned a qualification test*; they may not do Cody work.
- An HTTP 200 whose response names a **different** model is a FAILED
  qualification, recorded as such (the fleet has been burned by exactly
  this substitution pattern before).
- Qualification expires under the NEMO law: no logged completion in 7 days
  → back to PROPOSED until re-tested.
- **$0 only.** Qualification and production runs use free/already-connected
  lanes only. **No paid fallbacks.** If the only working route costs money,
  the job is BLOCKED_MODEL/BLOCKED_ACCESS with the cause stated — Cody
  does not quietly buy its way out.
- **No private code to unapproved providers.** Code, diffs, and repo
  content go only to providers/lanes already connected and approved in the
  fleet. Anonymous/stealth routes and any new provider are unapproved by
  default, whatever their catalog claims.

## 3. Pipeline stages

Every Cody work order moves through these stages. Stage changes are written
into the work-order file; a work order never skips Review or Verify.

1. **INTAKE** — Zane restates the ask in one paragraph, classifies it
   (task class, Level A/B/C), and names what "done" looks like. Level C
   elements are split out and queued for Brandon's tap immediately, not
   discovered mid-build.
2. **SPEC** — Work order created from `WORK_ORDER_TEMPLATE.md`:
   scope, non-goals, acceptance tests, evidence required, lane assignment,
   Claude justification (or "none"). Non-trivial architecture → Astra
   reviews the spec; Brandon approves by tap when the spec changes cost,
   scope, or direction.
3. **BUILD** — Builder works on a branch/worktree via OpenCodeX. Code and
   its tests land together. Max 2 heavy builds at once; the rest queue
   visibly in `missions/`.
4. **TEST** — Acceptance tests + existing suite run on the host. Output is
   pasted/linked into the work order. A red suite stops the pipeline —
   no "ship and fix later" without Brandon's word.
5. **REVIEW** — Council (or a non-builder lane) reviews the diff:
   correctness, scope creep, security, style of the codebase. Verdict:
   APPROVE / REWORK / REJECT, with reasons in the work order.
6. **VERIFY** — Themis independently re-runs the acceptance tests and
   checks every claim the builder made. Builder's logs are not evidence
   until re-run.
7. **SHIP** — Merge/deliver per the work order's ship definition. Draft PRs
   are Level A; publishing/merging to a live surface that Brandon or the
   public uses follows the fence in the work order (often Level C tap).
8. **RECEIPT** — War-room receipt in Brandon's format + work order closed
   with: what shipped, where, test results, review verdict, Claude calls
   used (count + purpose), remaining gaps stated plainly.

## 4. Quality gates (all must pass before SHIP)

- [ ] Producing model is **TESTED-qualified** (§2.3) — response model field
      from a logged real completion matches the claimed model
- [ ] **No static fixture output counted as a model-backed job** — fixture/
      stub/dry-run results, if any, are labeled and reported separately
      from model results (CHARTER §1.1, §4.1)
- [ ] Acceptance tests from the work order **run and pass** (output attached)
- [ ] Existing test suite for the touched area still passes (or pre-existing
      failures are named and proven pre-existing)
- [ ] No secrets in the diff (keys, tokens, passwords — checked, not assumed)
- [ ] Scope matches the work order; extra changes are listed or reverted
- [ ] Independent review verdict = APPROVE (reviewer ≠ builder)
- [ ] Verification re-run by Themis/Zane (verifier ≠ builder)
- [ ] Receipt written; Brandon-facing deliverable exists where promised
- [ ] Claude ledger updated if any Claude call was made

A gate that cannot run (e.g., suite needs egress) is marked **UNVERIFIED**
in the receipt — never silently treated as passed.

## 5. Integration with Genesis

- **Platinum:** Cody work orders inherit Platinum classification. Cody is a
  *consumer* of the Authority Engine, not a second authority: Level B
  actions go through existing approved playbooks + signed receipts;
  Cody cannot mint its own playbooks or approvals.
- **Genesis HQ:** Cody's intended HQ representation is a department panel:
  work orders in flight as missions, lane status from the supervisor/
  chain-tracer state, Claude-credit gauge from the ledger. **That panel is
  NOT built yet** — it is Starter Mission 3 (ARCHITECTURE-scale honesty:
  designed here, not claimed). Until then, `genesis-os/cody/` + war-room
  receipts are the record.
- **Supervisor:** the Genesis supervisor already owns the lane proxies
  (33 live services after the 2026-10-24 compile pass). Cody reads lane
  health from supervisor/chain-tracer state; Cody does not restart proxies
  itself except via PB-01 (approved playbook).
- **Engineer Team:** `genesis-os/engineer-team/TEAM.md` remains the
  historical roster record. Cody's charter supersedes it as the operating
  structure from 2026-10-24; lane *facts* are kept in sync here (§2.1).
- **Hermes / nanoMuse / other departments:** Cody assigns them work only
  through their existing seats and fences (Hermes drafts/stages, never
  sends; IT department owns platform upgrades; Ops owns live recovery).
  Cody coordinates — it does not absorb other departments' seats.
- **Money law:** Cody builds things that make money only inside Brandon's
  standing fences. Cody itself spends $0 and sells nothing on its own.

## 6. Hosting plan (honest)

| Phase | Host | What runs there | State |
|-------|------|-----------------|-------|
| Now | zane-box (this VM, 2 CPU / 8 GB) | Coordination, specs, local builds/tests, docs, local Ollama grunt lane. Survives VM recycles because all state is files in `genesis-os/cody/` — nothing lives only in a process | **LIVE (as a working method)** |
| Next | genesis-s1 (16 GB, Ubuntu 24.04) | Heavy builds, OpenCodeX sessions, larger local models, Cody's future build runner | **BLOCKED on path**: S1 completed `gh auth login` as brandonduda8 (photo-verified 2026-10-24); no fleet SSH path exists yet (box egress stalled; rendezvous/gh path is the designed bridge). No Cody component is installed on the S1 today |
| Later | penguin / burst (Kaggle/Colab) | Docker-capable builds on penguin; GPU work on burst lanes | On contact / per-run rules |

Rules that keep Cody alive on zane-box: state in files, not processes;
no Cody daemon required for correctness; every work order resumable from
its file after a recycle; local inference ceiling ≤1.5B class stays.

## 7. Failure modes Cody is designed for

- **Claude at zero credits** → router simply has no Claude row; department
  continues (Policy §5). Designed mode, rehearsed by Starter Mission 1.
- **Egress stall (current)** → local + browser-lane work proceeds; cloud
  work queues as STAGED with lanes named.
- **A builder lane silently degrades** → NEMO law: no logged completion in
  7 days = off the roster until re-proven with a real completion whose
  model field matches.
- **VM recycle mid-build** → work order file is the checkpoint; builder
  resumes or restarts from it; receipt notes the interruption honestly.
- **Reviewer unavailable** → work waits at REVIEW. Cody never self-approves
  to keep velocity. Brandon is told it's blocked, with the reason.

# CODY — Claude Credit Policy

**Effective:** 2026-10-24, on Brandon's word: *"Claude bill is due so we can
use whatever we have in Claude credits left."*
**Applies to:** every Claude call made for Cody engineering work — LiteLLM
routes `claude` (Sonnet) and `claude-audit` (Opus) via the Anthropic proxy
(:18792), and any other Claude surface used on Cody's behalf.
**Ledger:** `genesis-os/cody/state/claude_credit_ledger.json`
**Owner:** Zane (proposes + logs) · Brandon (approves above the small band).

> Honest basis: the fleet does **not** have a live, verified readout of the
> remaining Anthropic credit balance in this file, and Cody will not invent
> one. The balance is whatever Brandon's Anthropic console says. This policy
> therefore rations by **call class, call count, and estimated size** — the
> things Cody controls — and treats the balance as scarce until Brandon
> says otherwise.
>
> **Reachability assumption (2026-10-24): Claude is UNREACHABLE until proven
> otherwise.** WO-CODY-P0-EXECUTE-001 was staged to Claude via the bridge as
> `msg-0c4da07b6e9bb34bb941078273016d24`, status **PENDING_TRANSPORT** —
> Claude has **NOT acknowledged** it, and the Anthropic route is in
> EGRESS-HOLD besides. This policy therefore plans as if no Claude call can
> land today: no Cody work order may list Claude as a *dependency* (only as
> an optional, policy-gated escalation), and §8 zero-mode routing is the
> operating default until a real ack + a tested completion land.

---

## 1. The principle

Claude credits are **capital for judgment**, not fuel for production.
Every routine token Cody burns on Claude shortens the runway for the one
moment where Claude is the difference between shipping and being stuck.
Default answer to "should this go to Claude?" is **no**.

## 2. Allowed uses — the only three classes

| Class | Use | Shape of the call |
|-------|-----|-------------------|

## The system (Google's practices, fleet-sized)

1. **Design before build.** Anything bigger than a one-file fix gets a short
   design note first: goal, approach, risks, rollback. No design, no build.
2. **Builder ≠ reviewer ≠ verifier.** Cody (or Zane) builds. A different seat
   reviews. Zane verifies the receipt against reality before it counts.
   Nobody grades their own homework.
3. **Small, reviewable changes.** One purpose per change. If a change can't be
   described in two sentences, it's too big — split it.
4. **Tests or it didn't happen.** New code lands with a test or a documented
   manual proof. Existing tests must pass before and after. A failing test
   blocks the ship, not the report.
5. **Readability over cleverness.** Code is read by the next agent at 3 AM
   during an outage. Boring, named, commented-where-it-matters wins.
6. **Launch checklist, every ship.** Before anything goes live:
   - [ ] Works end-to-end from the user's side (not just the builder's side)
   - [ ] Restart-survival proven (service comes back on its own)
   - [ ] Rollback path exists and is written down
   - [ ] No new 0.0.0.0 listeners; no secrets in code, chat, or logs
   - [ ] Receipt written: what, where, proof, what's still open
7. **Blameless postmortems.** When something breaks or a claim turns out
   wrong: timeline, root cause, the fix, and the rule that prevents round two.
   The correction goes out in the same conversation the claim was made in.
8. **Health is a number, not a vibe.** Services report up/down/degraded from
   live probes. A dashboard shows records; it never invents them.
9. **Finish over start.** Work-in-progress limit: three priorities at a time.
   A new start requires a finish, a kill, or Brandon's explicit override.
   Started-and-stalled is the fleet's #1 defect and is treated as one.
10. **Receipts are files.** A chat summary is an index, not a delivery.
    Every finished job leaves a receipt file a fresh session can verify cold.

## How work flows

Brandon names the outcome → Zane scopes it (design note if needed) → Cody or
Zane builds in small changes → independent review → Zane verifies live →
receipt filed → Brandon sees it working in his hands. Anything less is
in-progress, and gets reported as in-progress.

Zane, as engineer of record, can block a ship that fails the checklist —
including his own work. Exceptions need Brandon's word, recorded in the
receipt.

# gensdk — Genesis Training SDK

One programmatic interface over all of Brandon Duda's GPU/TPU training
services. Built 2026-10-31 on Brandon's order ("make me a sdk... I'll sign
in and grant you admin access to all my GPU and tpu services"), immediately
after he lifted the per-run tap fence for free-lane training.

gensdk is the clean programmatic layer **over** the existing October
training system (`genesis-os/train/` — dispatchers, dashboard, envelope
gates, job queue) and the provider CLIs. It is not a competing system: job
fields and quota conventions mirror `train/` (service keys `kaggle_gpu`,
`kaggle_tpu`, `colab`, `lightning`; Kaggle quota in weekly hours; the
dataset SHA-256 hash-gate discipline). The coordinator's autopilot
(`genesis-os/training/`) launches runs; gensdk is what any agent or script
calls to stage, launch, check, and account for them.

## Design law

- **CLI wrappers only.** Each provider module shells out to the provider's
  own CLI (`bin/kaggle.py`, `colab-fixed`, `modal`). The SDK never
  reimplements provider auth and never reads, prints, logs, or persists
  any credential or token file. Kaggle auth is a Secure-Vault surrogate
  injected inside the connector CLI; Colab auth is the CLI's own OAuth
  store; Modal auth is `~/.modal.toml`, read by the Modal CLI alone.
- **Staging by default.** `gensdk submit <spec>` validates the spec,
  verifies the dataset hash gate, and writes a staging record. Nothing
  launches and nothing burns without `--execute`.
- **Policy engine before every launch** (`gensdk/policy.py`):
  - Free lanes (Kaggle GPU, Kaggle TPU, Colab included CUs, S1-local) are
    auto-approved under Brandon's 2026-10-31 order.
  - Modal auto-approves only while month-to-date Modal spend (gensdk
    ledger) plus the run's cap stays within the **$30/mo included
    credit**. Overage is paid spend — Brandon's tap, never automatic.
  - **Top-up purchases are never automatic.** There is no purchase code
    path anywhere in this SDK.
  - **One run per lane at a time**; an execute-submit refuses while the
    lane's active run is not terminal.
  - **Eval/quality gates are not taps** and are not waived: a spec's
    `eval_gate` travels with the run record and must pass before any
    downstream serving decision.
- **Burn ledger** (`ledger/burn-ledger.jsonl`): append-only JSONL; every
  append is read back from disk and verified before the call returns.
  `gensdk ledger` reports ISO-week and calendar-month totals per
  provider/unit. The ledger is the SDK's own book — provider-side truth
  is read live by `gensdk quota`.

# Genesis Pay S0 — owned ledger layer (v0.2.0)

Design of record: `genesis-os/war-room/GENESIS_POWER_PLAN_RE_2026-10-17.md` §5
(Claude components C1–C11 + invariants I-1…I-22). Commissioned by Brandon
2026-10-17 (Power Plan §9.3, “tap all”). Stdlib-only Python. $0, internal.

## What this is

S0 of the Genesis Pay sovereignty roadmap: **our own double-entry ledger +
payment-intent service + three-way reconciliation**, sitting *behind* Apex
Invoicing (which stays the system of record for what is owed) and *in front
of* a future orchestrator adapter (Hyperswitch at S2 — **not installed**;
Brandon's sandbox-or-defer choice is still open). Genesis Pay records truth
and prepares movements; **it never moves money** — there is deliberately no
send/execute adapter anywhere in the package.

## Layout

- `genesis_pay/core.py` — `GenesisPay` (ledger, intents, disputes, refunds,
  C8 tap gate, webhook ingestor, reconciliation, audit chain)
- `genesis_pay/errors.py` — fail-closed error types with HTTP-equivalent statuses
- `tests/test_genesis_pay.py` — 28 unit tests (all passing 2026-10-17)
- `demo.py` → `demo_output/demo_output.json` — fake-data end-to-end evidence
- Storage: a **dedicated SQLite file** per instance (never the live Apex DB)

## Money flow (state machine + journal)

1. Apex invoice issued → `ingest_invoice_issued` posts **Dr AR / Cr Revenue**
   and mirrors the invoice.
2. Apex payment **confirmed** (the Apex confirmation is Brandon's tap
   upstream; pending payments are refused) → **Dr Clearing:\<rail\> / Cr AR**,
   intent → `confirmed`.
3. Settlement → **Dr Bank cash (net) + Dr Fees / Cr Clearing (gross)**,
   intent → `settled`. The settlement carries its own external reference
   (`settlement:<intent>`) so one external ref maps to exactly one entry.
4. Void = a **new reversing entry** (Dr Revenue / Cr AR), never an edit.
5. Dispute opens → contested amount frozen at once (Dr Disputes-frozen /
   Cr Bank-or-Clearing). Won → funds return to the account the freeze drew
   from; lost → Dr Dispute losses / Cr Disputes-frozen.
6. Refund → only against an **approved Brandon tap request**, capped at the
   ledger level: captured − refunds − dispute losses.

## The C8 tap gate (outbound money movement = Brandon's tap)

`create_tap_request` only *creates* an immutable request bound to its
payload hash. `approve_tap_request` requires actor exactly `brandon`,
initiator ≠ approver (four-eyes), unexpired, and outside any
destination-change cooldown. `prepare_instruction` returns
`{status: "prepared_only", executed: false, adapter: null}` — a human
executes on the real rail and the outcome is recorded back with its
external reference. Destination changes invalidate the prior approval and
start a fresh request with a cooldown.

## Invariant mapping (Claude I-1…I-22, as summarized in Power Plan §5)

- **Idempotency (I-1…I-5):** client key required on every money call;
  key + payload hash + result stored in the same transaction as the
  journal/intent/outbox writes; exact replay returns the stored result;
  same key + different payload = `ConflictError` (409); internal retries
  reuse deterministic keys (settlement refs derive from the intent id).
- **Ledger integrity (I-6…I-11):** append-only journal/audit enforced by
  SQLite triggers; balanced double-entry only; integer minor units, no
  floats; explicit 3-letter currency per entry; every entry carries an
  external ref or is flagged `unmapped_flagged`; one external ref maps to
  exactly one entry.
- **Reconciliation (I-12…I-13):** three-way match (intents/ledger vs
  settlement report vs bank deposits) keyed by external ref; every break
  persists as an **open exception with owner + SLA**; breaks are never
  auto-closed and never fixed by editing the ledger.
- **State & safety (I-14…I-15, I-21…I-22):** strict forward-only intent
  state machine; webhooks are untrusted until HMAC-verified and are
  deduped by (provider, event_id); the system **fails closed**;
  UNKNOWN outcomes resolve only via an explicit `query_result` event.
- **Disputes & refunds (I-16…I-17):** disputes freeze the contested amount
  at notice; refunds are capped at captured − refunds − losses **in the
  ledger**, not by caller honesty.
- **Approvals (I-18…I-20):** server-side gate in `GenesisPay` (not a UI
  promise); four-eyes by construction; approvals bind to immutable
  payload hashes; destination changes cool off + re-approve.
- **Audit (C9):** hash-chained audit log (`verify_audit_chain()`), plus a
  transactional outbox of every domain event.

`genesis_pay/paylinks.py` + `rails_config.json`: one simple pay page per

Design law: link rails first, instruction rails where no public merchant
link scheme is verified, and **never a guessed URL**.

|---|---|---|
| Cash App | link `https://cash.app/$zanehart369` + QR | **VERIFIED** ($cashtag profile link; rail fleet-verified payable). The page shows the exact amount + invoice-number note beside the button. ## Zero-sum enforcement + durability (Argon RALPH-004 convergence)

Argon's WO-002 return (RALPH-004) independently specced the same core;
adopted deltas:

- **DB-level zero-sum trigger.** Entries declare `debit_total_cents`,
  `credit_total_cents`, and `line_count` at insert; the
  `journal_lines_zero_sum` trigger verifies the actual line sums against
  the declaration (and declared debit == declared credit) when the final
  line lands. Raw SQL writes that bypass the posting API are rejected by
  the database itself (proven by tests that write unbalanced rows
  directly). The posting-API balance check remains the first line of
  defense.
- **100-case simulation suite** (`tests/test_argon_acceptance.py`):
  100 deterministic invoice→payment→settlement cases across all rails
  with dispute-loss and tapped-refund slices mixed in; every case asserts
  exact bank/fees balances and **0-cent drift** (trial balance nets to
  exactly 0), plus unbalanced-entry rejection and the durability checks
  below. Written as unittest (pytest is not installed on this box;
  pytest collects unittest suites unchanged).
- **Durability:** file-backed ledgers open with `journal_mode=WAL` +
  `synchronous=FULL` — a committed posting survives power loss / VM
  recycle (this box recycles ~13×/day; the setting is asserted by test).
- **Not adopted:** Argon's `genesis_pay_router` naming and any framing
  of the SQLite ledger as a new invoicing stack. Apex Invoicing remains
  the invoicing system of record; Genesis Pay is the ledger *behind* it,
  per the Power Plan §5 design of record. Convergence is on the money
  invariants, not on replacing the stack.

# Genesis Vault v1

Personal-treasury records and a daily one-screen board, built to sit beside Genesis Pay. Python 3.10+, standard library only, $0, local.

**Genesis never moves money.** The Vault records what Brandon enters or imports from his own statements, then tells him what needs attention. Every transfer is Brandon's tap in the provider's app (invariant C8). There is no network or subprocess code in this package; a test enforces it. There is no server, so there is nothing to bind.

## Ledger discipline (same bar as Genesis Pay S0)

- Integer cents only. The cents columns have no SQLite type affinity, so the text `'5.00'` cannot silently become 5 cents. `parse_cents` refuses floats and anything below a cent.
- Double entry: an entry becomes posted only if it has 2+ postings that sum to zero (trigger). Postings are append-only, posted entries are immutable, and every write carries an idempotency key.
- A stated balance is booked against a `reconciliation` equity account, so the ledger total stays exactly 0.
- Hash-chained, append-only audit log (`verify_audit`, or the `audit-verify` command).
- `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=FULL`, `foreign_keys=ON`.

## The board

- **Deficit guard**: flags an account whose open outflows due within 14 days (or undated) exceed its balance. This is the Robinhood $5 bounce class. Accounts with no entered balance show `UNKNOWN_BALANCE`, and bills with no paying account show `UNASSIGNED`. Neither is silently treated as fine.
- **Bill calendar**: final notices first, then overdue, undated, and upcoming. An item stays open until Brandon records one outcome: `paid`, `arranged`, `disputed` or `cancelled`.
- **Sweep cards**: `PREPARED_ONLY` cards reading "Move $X from A to B", drawn from accounts with known surplus after their own bills and buffer. `NO_SOURCE` appears when nothing covers the gap. Cards are computed, never stored or executed.

## Use (from `pay/`)

```bash
DB=~/genesis-vault.db
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB seed-known            # 7 accounts (no balances) + Talkiatry $100 final notice
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB set-balance cash_app 43.12 --as-of 2026-10-30

python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB add-bill rh-1 "Robinhood debit" 5.00 --due 2026-11-01 --account robinhood --kind scheduled_debit
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB mark-outcome 1 arranged --note "payment plan"
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB record-transfer t-1 cash_app robinhood 5.00 --on 2026-10-30   # after Brandon did it in the app
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB board --html board.html
python3 -m genesis_vault --db $DB audit-verify
```

## Keepalive-spawned daemons: double-fork --daemon, never setsid, never bare nohup (2026-09-25, hard-won)- The workshop server flap-looped twice in one day (16:41–17:22 UTC, then 21:36–21:54 UTC): each instance died silently within ~4 min, no traceback, stdlib-only code, no OOM. The earlier "removing setsid fixed it" was COINCIDENTAL — the flap returned hours later with no setsid anywhere.
- Real mechanism: the runtime reaps finished cron/exec workers and their process groups aggressively; plain `nohup ... &` children stay in the worker's process group and get SIGKILLed minutes later. nohup only ignores SIGHUP — it does NOT leave the process group.

- Rule: any daemon that must outlive its launcher gets a `--daemon` double-fork mode. Bare `nohup ... &` is NOT durable on this box, whatever the old notes say.
- Keepalive post-start probes: give slow servers a real startup window — poll up to 90s, not a single 10s sleep, or the log fills with false "FAILED to start" lines (AgentOS/Uvicorn, 2026-09-26).
- **VM reboots ~13×/day, ~every 90–110 min (2026-09-27, diagnosed via Apollo receiver death investigation).** CORRECTION of the old "daily ~22:08 UTC" note: boot_log.jsonl shows ~13 reboots/day, each killing every daemon instantly; 12 of 13 recent "silent deaths" line up exactly with boot times. Every Python daemon dies because the VM restarts; the 5-min keepalives rebuild everything within minutes. ## PID files lie after PID reuse (2026-09-25, hard-won)
- `tailscaled-mgr.sh` refused to restart tailscaled because `kill -0 $(cat tailscaled.pid)` succeeded — but the PID had been reused by an unrelated `python3 /tmp/peep_mac_hunt.py`. Both tailscaled and the ws bridge were dead while their PID files pointed at the stranger. The tailnet was down and every tailnet-dependent service (apollo receiver, phone/chromebook SSH, voice bridge) was degraded.
- Rule: a PID file + `kill -0` is NOT proof. Verify identity: `tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/<pid>/cmdline` must show the expected binary. When restarting via the manager, delete a stale PID file first if the cmdline doesn't match — otherwise `start` exits "already running" and fixes nothing.
- Higher lesson: one dead daemon (tailscaled) silently took down the whole tailnet surface. When several tailnet things fail at once, check the daemon and the bridge before chasing each service.
- **`tailscaled-mgr.sh reset` wipes `tailscaled.state` and forces a fresh interactive login (Brandon's tap) — it is NOT a connectivity fix (2026-09-30, self-inflicted).** A flaky peer path (e.g. penguin unreachable, rx 0) needs `stop`+`start` (state preserved), never `reset`. The original muse-node login was interactive; no auth key is cached anywhere, so a reset = dead tailnet until Brandon re-approves the machine at the login URL from `tailscale up`.
- **Stale Tailscale login URLs:** after a state wipe, an approved-but-stale auth URL silently does nothing — the node keeps printing the OLD URL. After Brandon taps and the node still shows "Logged out.", regenerate a fresh link with `tailscale up --force-reauth` (preserves state, never `--reset`) and send HIM the new URL. Verified 2026-09-30: old `a/15c6811e016432` tap landed nowhere; fresh `a/22d8bbf01fff0` restored the node in one tap.
- **Tailscale rotates auth URLs on its own — never promise a link "stays good until tapped" (2026-10-01, own-the-miss).** While logged out, tailscaled re-runs `doLogin` and the control plane mints a fresh auth URL (observed: `a/188ca7fa2cc517` lived ~26 min, replaced by `a/12ba7a592c6436` with no script intervention — no cron runs `tailscale up`). The old URL dies silently; a tap on it lands nowhere. Always hand Brandon the URL from the FRESHEST `tailscaled-mgr.sh status`, tell him to tap it promptly, and re-verify the URL right before he taps — a link minted minutes ago may already be dead.

- `team-claude.sh <WO>` only ENQUEUES via `bin/claude-runs.py submit` (pre-assigned `--session-id`); cron `claude-runs-tick` (5m, one poll) launches the worker via `daemonize.py` and, if the run died with no `type:result` in the log, relaunches with `claude -p --resume <session_id>` (max 6 attempts; honors the load>6 gate). State: `state/runs/<slug>.{json,log,progress.md}`; old synchronous runner kept as `team-claude.legacy.sh`.
- Pattern for other lanes: pre-assign a session/run id, append FULL output to a file (not a pipe), record boot_id+PIDs (verify by cmdline), treat "dead + no terminal result" as resumable, launch only from the tick. Resume needs the same cwd (claude stores sessions per-cwd) and the same flags re-passed.
- The bridge's `exec 9>` lock fd leaks into every builder tool shell; launch daemons with `9>&-`/close_fds or they hold the bridge lock forever.

## Keepalive false-kill pattern: load storm vs dead service (2026-09-29, diagnosed live)
- Apex Invoicing died ~30x in 24h and 4x in 30 min with ZERO crash tracebacks in server.log. Root cause was NOT the server: box at load ~12 on 2 CPUs starved the keepalive's own 15s curl probe, the probe timed out (HTTP 000), and the keepalive murdered a HEALTHY server — then restarted it into the same storm. "The keepalive becomes the outage."
- Same day, the workshop keepalive's 3s probe failed during the storm, restarted, and triggered the documented port-walk-up race (two writers, config drift) — the false kill was the first domino.
- Fix applied to both keepalives (reversible, $0): (1) probe timeout raised (apex 15s→30s, workshop 3s→15s); (2) load gate — if 1-min load > 8, never restart on a probe timeout, log and let the next poll retry; (3) workshop: if :$PORT is listening but the HTTP probe failed, skip the restart (no duplicate writers).
- General rule: before "restarting" anything, distinguish a dead process from a starved probe — check `ss -ltn` for the listener and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for the process. A probe timeout under high load is evidence about the LOAD, not about the service.
- Load-gate refinement (2026-09-29): the load gate can now misclassify a REAL death as a starved probe — apex server was provably dead (stale PID 4177, no 18811 listener, curl exit 7 refused) while the keepalive declined restart "under load storm". Proposed hardening (not applied): when the load gate fires, still restart if the process is provably dead — no /proc/<pid> AND no listener AND curl exit 7 (refused). A curl timeout (exit 28) stays a skip. Matches the workshop-keepalive block the same afternoon (port 18805 dark, no restart, load 13.66).
detail: section: Keepalive false-kill pattern: load storm vs dead service (2026-09-29, diagnosed live)

## Bulk I/O discipline on the 2-core VM (2026-09-27, WO-CLAUDE-008)
- **Never recursive-grep `~/workspace`.** Use `rg` with an excludes file (models/, kaggle-kernels/,
  backups/, node_modules/, vendor/). A 16-min recursive grep over 62GB at load 11+ is how the box
  ends up unusable.
- **Bulk I/O runs under `nice -n 19 ionice -c3`** (backups, scans, uploads). No exceptions.
- **No builder dispatch while 1-min load > 6.** Check first, queue instead.
- **My own dispatch pattern:** never pipe a builder run through `| tail -30` again — full stdout goes
  to `state/runs/<WO>.log`, and I tail the file. (The audit caught me throwing away the evidence.)
- A background `for i in seq; do poll; sleep 600; done` loop WILL be SIGKILLed when the runtime GCs the finished tool call's cgroup (same root cause as the proxy deaths — verified 2026-09-23: the phoenix v7 monitor died after poll 1, leaving a stale "RUNNING" log line for 2h while the kernel was actually ERROR).
- Pattern for watching anything long-lived: a cron that does ONE poll per run and exits. Terminal state (COMPLETE/ERROR) is recorded in the log + state file and the loop stops itself. Never trust a monitor log line older than the cron interval — verify against the live source.
- **pkill -f footgun:** the pattern matches your own shell's cmdline. Use the bracket trick: `pkill -f "[d]ockerd"`.
- **The bracket trick must cover EVERY literal in the pattern, and kill/start go in separate calls (2026-10-04, self-inflicted x2).** `pkill -f 'a2a_gateway'` killed my own shell twice in one session — the pattern text sits in the shell's own arguments. And `pkill -f 'x[.]py'` in a line that ALSO contains `nohup python3 .../x.py --daemon` still self-matches, because the restart half carries the unbracketed literal. Rule: bracket every literal (`[a]2a_gateway`), and never put the kill and the restart in the same command line.
- **pkill --echo is NOT a dry run (2026-09-29, self-inflicted):** `--echo` prints the matched command but pkill still delivers the signal — a "verify with pkill --echo" one-liner killed the healthy reel-studio serve process. For identity checks, read /proc/<pid>/cmdline; never pkill to inspect.
detail: section: Bulk I/O discipline on the 2-core VM (2026-09-27, WO-CLAUDE-008)

text: - **NEVER `pkill -f ""` (2026-09-27, self-inflicted outage).** An empty pattern matches EVERYTHING the user can signal — it SIGTERMs the whole box (apex server, every model proxy, your own shell). Zane did this during the apex-invoicing keepalive and took down the fleet; the 5-min keepalives rebuilt most of it within ~2 min, and the rest (gemini, openrouter) were manually kicked via their own keepalive scripts. There is no legitimate use of a blanket pkill. Kill by verified PID (check /proc/<pid>/cmdline first) or not at all.

## Downloads through the egress proxy: verify, don't trust (2026-09-26, hard-won)
- urllib through the proxy can return a TRUNCATED read as clean EOF — `r.read()` returns b"" early with no IncompleteRead raised, so the skill's 3x retry loop never fires and you get a silently corrupt file (observed: Kaggle kernel harvest with vectors.npy/idf.npy/manifest.json all truncated at random points, twice).
- Rule: every downloaded artifact gets a validity check (np.load shape, json parse, checksum) before use. curl is the safer downloader here — it exits 18 on partial transfer. When a file fails validation, re-fetch with curl and re-validate until clean.
- Kaggle harvests (2026-09-26, verified): `kaggle.py output` (ListKernelSessionOutput + urllib on signed URLs) truncates silently through the proxy — adapter 4.9MB short, tokenizer 5.5MB short, run_report cut mid-string, zero exceptions raised. Re-fetch each broken file with curl against a FRESH signed URL (fetch URL + curl in one call; old ones 404 within minutes). Status polling: kernels/list returns stub entries with status=? — ground truth is the ListKernelSessionOutput RPC file list + log tail (nbconvert __results__.html write = end-of-run marker). GetKernelSessionStatus/GetKernel RPCs 403 on this token (kernels.get denied).

## Keepalive probe timeouts: the 10s functional probe was the killer (2026-09-26, diagnosed live)
- At ~03:11-03:21Z a flap killed most proxies; keepalives restarted them, then
  IMMEDIATELY kept killing the healthy replacements: the functional probe used
  `curl --max-time 10`, but cold-start upstream egress latency was 25-45s
  (measured: groq /v1/models 200 in 24.9s, zai 40.7s). "Listening but failing
  functional probe" -> kill -> restart -> still slow -> kill... a 5-minute
  death loop across groq, zai, nvidia, gemini.
- Fix applied to all six *_proxy_keepalive.sh: (1) cold-start grace — skip the
  functional probe entirely when the pidfile process is <180s old; (2) probe
  timeout raised 10s -> 90s (anthropic 20s -> 90s). A slow 200 is a PASS; only
  502/000/hang means the proxy itself is broken. Verified: groq keepalive now
  exits 0 without touching a 50s-old healthy proxy.
- Rule: a functional probe's timeout must exceed the worst measured cold-start
  latency with margin, or the keepalive becomes the outage.

## Egress MITM CA rotates — long-lived TLS processes go stale (2026-09-26, hard-won)
- The egress proxy's MITM CA ROTATES (bundle `/run/hatch/egress-tls/ca-bundle.pem` replaced, observed 08:46 UTC). A Python process started before a rotation keeps its old CA in the SSL context: the socket stays listening but every upstream call 502s with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
- A keepalive that only checks "is the port listening" will NEVER self-heal this — the process looks alive. Keepalives for TLS proxies must do a FUNCTIONAL probe (e.g. GET /v1/models expecting 200) and restart on failure.
- Applied 2026-09-26: openrouter_proxy_keepalive.sh now probes `http://127.0.0.1:18790/v1/models` for HTTP 200; on mismatch it pkill-restarts the proxy. Same pattern applied the same morning to gemini, nvidia, and anthropic keepalives after all three went stale (18789/18791: GET /v1/models must be 200; 18792: POST /v1/messages must return a well-formed upstream error like 400, not 502). Anthropic is UP but UNFUNDED (400 "credit balance is too low") — that's the account's standing state, not a proxy bug.
- RULE: any long-lived TLS client behind the egress proxy gets a functional-probe keepalive, never a port check alone.

## The LiteLLM proxy was dying to worker-group SIGTERM, not flapping (2026-09-26, diagnosed)
- The proxy kept "shutting down" gracefully minutes after start. The keepalive launched it via `nohup ... &` + `disown`, which does NOT leave the launching cron worker's process group — the runtime reaps finished workers' process groups and the proxy ate the SIGTERM.

- Rule: EVERY long-lived daemon gets the double-fork treatment, including ones launched from keepalive crons. nohup+disown is never enough on this box.
- Same session also: pg_tunnel died ~06:32 UTC from an unexplained cause (last log: egress-proxy CONNECT refused); keepalive restarts it if 5433 goes quiet, which self-healed on next run. If tunnel deaths recur, investigate the egress proxy flapping.
- Applied the unapplied Prisma migration `20260729000000_add_reload_tracking_to_litellm_config` manually (columns `last_run_at`, `reload_revision` on LiteLLM_Config). It was marked applied in `_prisma_migrations` but the DDL never ran — the recurring `_check_and_reload_model_cost_map` ERROR is now gone.

It went stale 2026-09-27 because nothing invoked the probe — the WO-GEMINI-009 verification itself was the last writer. Fixed: cron `lane-health-probe` every 15m runs the probe (runtime-managed crons survive the ~13x/day reboots, so the cron IS the reboot-safe writer).
- Probe lanes (15 as of 2026-10-01, one 1-token real completion each through the runner's own proxy+model): claude (precondition), codex (NEEDS_LOGIN), goose (groq 120b), groq20 (groq 20b), gemini (flash-lite), gemma (gemma-4-26b via :18789, wired 2026-10-01), qwen (groq qwen3.8-27b chat backup), glm, ollama (local qwen2.5:1.5b), nvidia (NIM trial — was "known hang", now answering READY; old note retired), llm7 (READY), mistral (READY), apodex (apodex-1.1-mini:free via :18790 openrouter proxy, wired 2026-10-01 on Brandon's "add it to the team" tap), github-models (DORMANT — PAT landed upstream 2026-09-27), deepseek (DOWN:unfunded-top-up-required), anthropic (unfunded → DOWN:unfunded, honest standing state).

- Follow-up not done: health_dashboard SLO #2 (lane real-call success) still doesn't read lane_health.json — separate WO.
- **worker-bridge.sh probe breaks when /tmp is full (2026-09-28).** The probe does `curl -o "$(mktemp)"`; with /tmp at 100%, body writes fail → curl exit 23 → the script maps it to `*-proxy-unreachable`, a FALSE negative for every lane even when all proxies are healthy. /tmp/athena (root-owned Athena LoRA artifacts, 509MB) is the usual filler and is off-limits to touch. Workaround for a truthful run: `TMPDIR=~/workspace/tmp bash ~/workspace/bin/worker-bridge.sh probe` — but a second run inside the 10-min cache TTL just echoes the stale false results, so bust the cache first (move the JSON aside, it's the cron's own file). ## Bridge mailbox push mechanics (2026-09-30, self-inflicted)
- `mailbox.py push` scans ONLY top-level `bridge/outbox/*.json`. Files in per-recipient subdirs (`outbox/claude/`, `outbox/astra/`) are NEVER pushed — they sit there silently looking sent. Stage envelopes directly at top level.
- `envelope_sha256` must be computed over `bridge.canonical_envelope(env)` = `json.dumps(env, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)`. Default `json.dumps` separators/spacing produce a different hash and the HASH_GUARD refuses the push. Don't hand-roll it.
- Evidence this bit us: the WO-AURUM-007 decisions "relayed to Claude" at 05:17Z sat unpushed in `outbox/claude/` for ~40 min until discovered; the far end never saw it.
- **Wrong staged shape = nested envelope_sha256 (2026-10-02).** A hand-staged outbox file `{"envelope": {..., "envelope_sha256": ...}}` (hash nested inside the envelope, no top-level record fields) makes `mailbox.py push` fail HASH_GUARD with `envelope_sha256 None != recomputed <hash>`. Fix: rebuild the record as `{"envelope": env, "envelope_sha256": sha256(canonical_envelope(env)), "status": "PENDING_TRANSPORT", "transport": None, "staged_at": now}` with the `envelope_sha256` key REMOVED from inside the envelope. The hash value itself survives unchanged (content was never corrupt). After fixing, verify no other staged files share the defect before re-running push, then confirm the repo copy's hash matches.

## hatch_gws_cli Gmail CLI needs IPv6 egress proxy (2026-10-07)
- `hatch_gws_cli gmail` API calls fail with "error sending request for url" (or stall) on the default proxy env: the Go binary resolves `hatch-egress-proxy` to the IPv4 blackhole `198.19.0.1` (which is also in no_proxy, so it bypasses the proxy and dies direct). curl works; the CLI does not.
- Fix: point proxy vars at the IPv6 address directly: `PY='http://hatch-runtime:<cred>@[fd8b:4f84:7d32:99::1]:3128'` then export HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (upper+lower). Same class of failure as Java's (see Java section).
- Wrapper: `~/workspace/goals/apex-forge-empire-build/hidden_files/gws.sh` (0700 — the proxy URL embeds the egress credential).
- Note: CLI's first probe `hatch_gws_cli gmail accounts` works offline (no network), so a working `accounts` + failing API calls = proxy/DNS issue, not a Gmail disconnect.
- **Consumers of the CLI must go through the wrapper, not the bare binary (2026-10-08).** maya's `genesis-os/maya/sweep.py` called `hatch_gws_cli` directly and every sweep hung/timed out; fixed to exec the gws wrapper path by default (overridable via `HATCH_GWS_CLI` env). Any other cron/script that shells out to `hatch_gws_cli` (apex-reply-ingest et al.) needs the same treatment or it dies on the IPv4 blackhole.
- **The egress proxy credential ROTATES — gws.sh embeds a stale one (2026-10-09, bitten live).** The wrapper's hardcoded password stopped matching the live `$https_proxy` credential (sha mismatch), so API calls failed with "error sending request" until a fresh URL was built from the live env (`urlsplit(os.environ['https_proxy']).password` + IPv6 host). If the wrapper suddenly dies again, diff its credential hash against the live env before chasing anything else. Durable fix (not yet applied): wrapper should rebuild the URL from the live env at each invocation instead of embedding a credential.
- **HTTPS CONNECT through the IPv6 proxy can be extremely slow (~15–25s/request, 2026-10-09).** TCP connects instantly and plain-HTTP is fast; only CONNECT tunnels crawl. The Go CLI's internal timeout fires before the tunnel completes → treat "error sending request" on a healthy connection as "slow egress, retry with patience", not a broken CLI. Give long yields; the proxy warms up after the first successful tunnel.

## PATH shims must never symlink over the name the target execs (2026-10-07, self-inflicted)
- gws.sh ends with `exec hatch_gws_cli "$@"`. I made /tmp/gwsbin/hatch_gws_cli a SYMLINK to gws.sh, then `cat >` into it — the write followed the link and destroyed the real gws.sh (0700, held a credential). Two compounding failures: (1) symlink-over-exec-name write = clobber; (2) even as a symlink it caused infinite exec-recursion (gws.sh's `exec hatch_gws_cli` re-resolved to the shim via PATH).
- Rule: a PATH shim for a wrapper must be a REAL script that strips itself from PATH (PATH=${PATH//\/tmp\/shimdir:/}) before exec'ing the wrapper by absolute path — no symlinks, no credential copies.
- Repaired: restored gws.sh byte-identical (0700) and verified live. Incident + needed durable fix for the apex-reply-ingest cron (bare `hatch_gws_cli` dies on the IPv4 blackhole; needs the wrapper's IPv6 proxy env) logged in ~/memory/2026-10-07.md.

- **False-down probes when stdin is an open pipe (2026-10-09, root-caused live).** The keepalive probe reported penguin DOWN for 77 straight runs while penguin was UP the whole time. Cause: the probe ran chromebook-ssh without stdin redirect; the wrapper's stdin-buffering read (added 2026-10-08) blocks forever on an open non-EOF stdin (cron/worker context), so each probe burned its 180s timeout then recorded down. Fix: every chromebook-ssh call inside a script MUST carry `< /dev/null` — the TOOLS.md "from agents" guidance applies equally to cron scripts, and any script without it reports false "down" instead of failing loudly. Audit every cron/script that shells out to chromebook-ssh.
- **fleet-sweeper-probe.sh audit (2026-10-09):** both SSH probes were missing `< /dev/null` — patched both. ALSO: the phone's `df` is toybox and rejects `-B1` (`df: Unknown option 'B1'`), so the phone probe silently failed forever (phone falsely "unreachable" since Oct 5). Phone probe now uses plain `df` (1K blocks × 1024 → bytes). Verified: phone came back reachable 62% in 6.9s. Penguin verified genuinely unreachable at audit time (45s timeout even through the hardened wake path — dozing).

- **curl loopback probes need `--noproxy '*'` (2026-10-09).** curl honors `$http_proxy`/`$https_proxy` env and routes even 127.0.0.1 through the egress proxy (which denies loopback), so a plain `curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/...` returns HTTP:000 while the service is actually healthy. Always pass `--noproxy '*'` for localhost probes.

## openclaw_keepalive: debounce transient failures, flock against overlap (2026-10-10)
- The 5-min keepalive paged CONFIG_INVALID several times a night while the config was always healthy on immediate recheck — `node openclaw.mjs config validate` takes ~40s on a loaded box and ~2min when hot, beating the 150s timeout. Single-transient-failure pages are noise.
- Fix in `genesis-os/tools/openclaw_keepalive.sh`: `page_or_flake` helper — a lone failure logs `*_FLAKE` and exits 0; only TWO CONSECUTIVE failures with the same state page (exit 1). Match is on the state name only, so drifting detail values (gemini=0/1) can't suppress a real page. Validate timeout raised 150→240s. Plus an `flock -n` overlap guard so a slow poll never stacks behind the 5m cron cadence (SKIP_OVERLAP exits 0).
- Verified live: full script run exit 0 (~63s, wrote OK); synthetic two-run sequence proved flake→page→reset-after-OK semantics for CONFIG_INVALID and BACKEND_DOWN.
